mainTopic: Tied bundles and other doubtful materials as סכך, and when stalks count as ידות (handles) of food
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier discussion: the גמרא emends a ברייתא so that something is unfit only if it was as small as its leftover from the start. Next comes the rule against using tied bundles as סכך. מרימר allows the reed bundles of סורא, which are tied only for counting. רבי אבא allows willow huts once the top ties are undone. רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע each defend this, the second by teaching that a tie not meant for carrying is not a real אגד. רבי אבא then quotes שמואל: the vegetables used for מרור count as empty air in a סוכה, because they crumble when they dry. Two versions of רב הונא follow about ידות (handles): grapes picked for wine, or grain cut for סכך. The גמרא asks whether this matches a dispute between תנאים in a ברייתא about branches with fruit on them. רב מנשיא answers that the ברייתא is about grain first cut for food. The גמרא then challenges whether a change of mind can cancel the first intention, and it begins quoting a משנה about vessels that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Emending the ברייתא: Unfit Only When It Starts as Small as Its Leftover
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא fixes the wording of a ברייתא from the previous discussion. It now reads: it is unfit only when its beginning is as small as its remnant, namely one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say this: it is unfit only when its beginning, like its remnants, is one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing an earlier discussion that began on the previous amud. It solves a problem in a ברייתא by changing how we read it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original wording of the ברייתא caused a difficulty, so the גמרא says 'אלא אימא': read it differently. In the new reading, a bundle that shrinks down to a small leftover is still fine. It is unfit only if it was that small (a single item) from the very start.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say: a formula for changing the reading of a source
its beginning, meaning its original state
its remnants, meaning what is left over

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the discussion on the previous amud. It is not about the סכך bundles that come next, so do not try to connect it to מרימר.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is changing the wording of the ברייתא here, so read it this new way.

phrases.english: [it is unfit only] when its beginning
is like its remnants: one.
phrases.notes: Only if it started out as small as the leftover

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes the discussion earlier by emending the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to make it unfit in a case where it should be fine.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is unfit only if it started out as small as its leftover (one).

steps.title: מרימר: The Reed Bundles of סורא May Be Used as Roofing
steps.stepSummary: מרימר teaches that the reed bundles sold in סורא are valid סכך. They are tied only so they can be counted easily, so the tie does not make them a real bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר taught: These bundles of reeds from סורא may be used to roof the סוכה. Even though they are tied, they are tied only for counting.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. מרימר rules that certain tied reed bundles are still allowed as סכך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tied bundles (חבילות) are normally not allowed as סכך. מרימר says the purpose of the tie matters. A tie made only to count the reeds for sale is temporary, because the buyer will untie them, so it is not a real bundle.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main principle of the section: what matters is why a bundle was tied, not only the fact that it is tied.

phrases.english: Mareimar expounded:
these reed bundles of Sura —
one may roof [the sukka] with them.
Even though they are tied —
phrases.notes: The גמרא is answering a question you might be about to ask.

phrases.english: it is merely for counting that they are tied.
phrases.notes: The tie is temporary, so it is not a real bundle

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: tied bundles as סכך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Reed bundles tied only for counting are valid סכך.

steps.title: רבי אבא: Willow-Branch Huts Are Valid Once the Top Ties Are Undone
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא rules that huts made of willow branches can be used as סכך once the ties at their top are undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: These huts made of willow branches, once their top ties are undone, are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: A second ruling about tied materials. רבי אבא allows willow huts as סכך after the top ties are loosened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These huts are branches tied together at the top to form a cone shape. Once the top ties are released, the branches no longer form a tied bundle at the top, so רבי אבא calls them כשרין (valid).

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
these huts of willow branches,
once their top ties are undone —
they are valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling about another kind of tied material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Willow huts are valid סכך once their top ties are undone.

steps.title: Challenge: They Are Still Tied at the Bottom
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the willow huts are still tied at the bottom, so they should still count as a bundle.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they are still tied at the bottom!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Undoing the top ties is not enough if the branches are still tied below. A tie anywhere should seemingly keep them a bundle, which is invalid as סכך.

phrases.english: But they are tied from below!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אבא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבא's ruling that the huts are valid once the top ties are undone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bottom ties remain, so the branches are still a bundle.

steps.title: רב פפא: The Bottom Is Untied Too
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that רבי אבא was talking about a case where the bottom ties are also undone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a case where he unties them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends רבי אבא by narrowing the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב פפא, untying the top alone is not enough. רבי אבא meant that the bottom is untied as well, so no tie remains anywhere.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
[It is a case] where he unties them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אבא allowed the huts even while the bottom stays tied.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are valid only when the bottom is untied as well.

steps.title: רב הונא: A Tie Not Meant for Carrying Is Not a Tie
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers differently. Even if the bottom stays tied, it does not matter, because a tie that is not made for carrying the bundle is not considered a tie.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע said: Even if you say he does not untie them, any tie that is not made for carrying is not called a tie.
steps.whatsHappening: A second, different answer to the challenge. It keeps רבי אבא's ruling even when the bottom is still tied.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא gives a general rule: a tie counts as an אגד only if it holds the bundle together so it can be carried. Once the top is loose, the huts would fall apart if lifted. So the bottom tie does not make them a bundle.

keyTerms.meaning: even if you say: introduces an alternative answer

steps.whatToRemember: An אגד that invalidates סכך is a tie that makes the material into a carryable bundle. Ties made only for counting (מרימר), or that cannot be used to carry the bundle (רב הונא), do not count.
steps.confusionAlert: רב הונא does not disagree with רב פפא about the halacha of fully untied huts. He argues that even the half-untied case is valid.

phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua said:
Even if you say he does not untie them,
any tie that is not made for carrying it —
is not called a tie.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to רב פפא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining the concept (what counts as אגד)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any remaining tie makes the material a bundle.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a tie made for carrying counts as an אגד.

steps.title: Bitter-herb vegetables carry impurity but act like empty air
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes שמואל: the vegetables used for מרור on פסח spread טומאה under them but do not block it, and in a סוכה they count as empty air.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said in the name of שמואל: the vegetables that the חכמים said a person can use to fulfill his obligation on פסח spread impurity, do not block impurity, and invalidate a סוכה because they count as air.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רבי אבא, quoting שמואל. It gives three rules about the soft, leafy vegetables used for מרור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rule 1: if these vegetables form a covering over a source of טומאת מת, the impurity spreads to things underneath them. Rule 2: they cannot act as a barrier that stops the impurity from rising past them. Rule 3: in a סוכה they are treated like an empty gap in the roof, so a large enough area of them (three טפחים) invalidates the סוכה, the same way a gap of empty air would.

keyTerms.meaning: Vegetables. Here it means the soft, leafy kinds used for מרור.
They bring or spread impurity to what is under them
Block or act as a barrier
Empty air, an open gap in the סכך

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds like a contradiction: they spread טומאה but do not block it. They are strong enough to act as a covering that spreads impurity, but the חכמים did not let them count as a real barrier. Both rules lean toward strictness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects to the theme of the sugya: what kinds of material can count as real סכך. These vegetables are not even treated as a bad covering. They are treated as if nothing is there at all.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said that Shmuel said:
Vegetables about which the Sages said

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם יוֹצֵא בָּהֶן יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ בַּפֶּסַח,
phrases.english: a person fulfills his obligation with them on Passover,
phrases.notes: These are the vegetables that can be used for מרור.

phrases.english: they bring (spread) impurity,
phrases.notes: As a covering over a corpse, they spread its impurity to things beneath them.

phrases.english: and they do not block impurity,
and they invalidate a sukkah because of air.
phrases.notes: They are treated like an empty gap in the roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new statement by רבי אבא, placed after his earlier ruling about willow huts in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vegetables used for מרור spread טומאה, do not block it, and count as empty air in a סוכה.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why these vegetables are treated as if they are not there.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא is asking for the reason behind שמואל's ruling, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The puzzle is that the vegetables are a real, physical covering. So why should a סוכה covered with them be treated like open air? The גמרא wants the logic behind that.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why these vegetables count as empty air rather than as a real covering.

steps.title: They crumble when dry, so they count as absent
steps.stepSummary: Because these vegetables crumble and fall apart once they dry, they are treated as already gone, even while they are still fresh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, when they dry out, they crumble and fall, they are treated as if they are not there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 8. These vegetables do not last.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even while fresh, the vegetables are judged by what they will soon become: crumbs that fall away, so they are treated as if they are not there now. This explains why they do not block טומאה and why they count as air in a סוכה. It does not explain the first rule (that they spread טומאה), which is a separate stringency that stands apart from this reason.

keyTerms.meaning: They are like something that is not there

steps.whatToRemember: The vegetables used for מרור count as empty air in a סוכה, because they will crumble once they dry.

phrases.english: since when they dry
they crumble and fall,
they are like something that is not there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because they crumble when dry, they are treated as absent even while fresh.

steps.title: Grapes picked for the winepress have no handles
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes רב הונא: grapes picked to make wine have no ידות, so their stems do not take on or pass on impurity.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבא said in the name of רב הונא: one who picks grapes for the winepress, they have no handles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement from רבי אבא, this time quoting רב הונא. It is about grape stems.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the stem of a food counts as a 'handle' (יד). A handle can become impure and pass that impurity to the food, or pick it up from the food. But a winemaker does not want the stems, so here they lose the status of a handle. They are just waste.

keyTerms.meaning: Handles: stems or attached parts that count with the food for impurity

steps.confusionAlert: ידות here does not mean human hands. It means the stems or stalks attached to a food, which the הלכה treats as part of it for טומאה.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said:
One who picks grapes for the winepress —
it has no handles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another statement by רבי אבא, brought because the previous one was also his.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grapes picked for the winepress have no ידות.

steps.title: Grain cut for סכך has no handles
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר גדא quotes רב הונא differently: grain cut to be used as סכך has no ידות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב מנשיא בר גדא said in the name of רב הונא: one who cuts grain for סכך, it has no handles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב הונא's teaching. In this version the case is grain cut for a סוכה roof, not grapes for wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person cutting the grain wants the stalks for his roof, not the grain. So the stalks are not treated as handles attached to the food. That means they do not join the grain for טומאה, which makes them suitable as סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: One who cuts or harvests grain
The roof covering of a סוכה

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: And Rav Menashya bar Gadda said that Rav Huna said:
One who cuts grain for roofing —
it has no handles.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different version of the same teaching from רב הונא, about a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Grain cut for סכך has no ידות.

steps.title: The grain version surely agrees about grapes
steps.stepSummary: Whoever says grain cut for סכך has no handles would certainly say the same about grapes for wine, because the winemaker actively does not want the stems.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says this about cutting grain would surely say it about picking grapes, because he does not want the stems, so that they will not absorb his wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now compares the two versions from steps 10 and 11. It starts by showing that the grain version includes the grape case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The winemaker's case is the stronger one. The stems actually hurt him, because they soak up wine. So if the stalks of grain lose handle status even though they do no harm, grape stems surely do.

keyTerms.meaning: He is not pleased with it, he does not want it

phrases.english: The one who said this about cutting grain,
all the more so about picking grapes —
since he does not want the stems,
so that they will not absorb his wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹצֵר כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן בּוֹצֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts comparing the two versions of רב הונא's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The grain version also holds that grapes picked for wine have no ידות, all the more so.

steps.title: The grape version may hold that grain does have handles
steps.stepSummary: Whoever says only grapes for wine have no handles might hold that grain cut for סכך does have handles, because the attached grain helps weigh down the stalks.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says that picking grapes has no handles may hold that cutting grain does have handles, because he wants to roof with them so that the stalks do not scatter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the comparison. The grape version does not automatically include the grain case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the grain case, the person may actually want the grain left on. It adds weight, so the wind does not blow the stalks away. Since the grain is useful to him, the stalks may still count as handles. So the two versions truly disagree about grain cut for סכך.

keyTerms.meaning: He is pleased with it, he wants it

steps.whatToRemember: Whether a stem counts as a handle depends on whether the person wants it. Grape stems are unwanted for wine, so both versions agree they are not handles. For grain cut for סכך, the versions disagree, because the grain may be wanted to keep the stalks from blowing away.

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר בּוֹצֵר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יָדוֹת,
phrases.english: The one who said that picking grapes has no handles,
but cutting grain does have handles —
since he wants to roof with them,
so that they will not scatter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר בּוֹצֵר שֶׁאֵין לוֹ יָדוֹת אֲבָל קוֹצֵר יֵשׁ לוֹ יָדוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison begun in step 12 by showing the other direction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both versions agree that grape stems are not handles. They disagree about grain cut for סכך, because the grain may be useful for weighing down the stalks.

steps.title: Is רב מנשיא's view an old dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that רב מנשיא בר גדא's ruling is really the subject of an argument between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that the view of רב מנשיא בר גדא is a dispute among the תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It suggests that the argument about סכך and ידות already appears among the תנאים, and it will bring a ברייתא to show this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we had two אמוראים quoting רב הונא differently. Now the גמרא asks whether רב מנשיא's version (grain cut for סכך has no ידות) is a point that the תנאים already argued about. If it is, then רב מנשיא sides with one תנא and רבי אבא sides with the other.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say. Introduces a suggestion the גמרא will test.
It is a dispute among the תנאים.
The אמורא who said that grain cut for סכך has no ידות.

phrases.english: Shall we say that the view of Rav Menashya bar Gadda
is a dispute of Tannaim?

steps.triggerLanguage: נֵימָא דְּרַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר גַּדָּא תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining how the two versions of רב הונא differ, the גמרא looks for the same argument among the תנאים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does רב מנשיא's ruling depend on one side of an argument between תנאים?

steps.title: The ברייתא about branches with fruit on them
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules on סכך made of branches or stalks that still have food attached. The תנא קמא compares waste to food. אחרים require the straw to be more than the ידות and the food combined.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: fig branches with figs on them, vines with grapes on them, straw with grain on it, and palm branches with dates on them. For all of these, if the waste is more than the food, the סוכה is kosher. If not, it is not kosher. אחרים say: it is not kosher until the straw is more than the ידות and the food together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about סכך that still has fruit or grain attached. The two views in it will be used to show an argument about ידות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Food can become טמא, and anything that can become טמא may not be used as סכך. The תנא קמא only compares waste against food, so he seems to treat the ידות as plain waste. אחרים add the ידות to the food side, so they seem to treat the ידות as part of the food.

keyTerms.meaning: Vine branches or grape clusters on their stems.
Waste. The inedible part, which is kosher as סכך.
"Others." An unnamed תנא, identified as רבי מאיר.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two meanings of פסולת here. In this ברייתא, פסולת means "waste" (the kosher part for סכך). The word פסולה means "unfit." They look alike but mean opposite things in this context.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
Fig branches with figs on them,
vines with grapes on them,
straw with stalks of grain on it,
palm branches with dates on them,

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלָּן, אִם פְּסוֹלֶת מְרוּבָּה עַל הָאוֹכָלִין — כְּשֵׁרָה,
phrases.english: for all of them, if the waste is more than the food, it is kosher,
and if not, it is unfit.
Acherim say:
Not unless the straw is more
than the handles and the food together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source text for the suggestion in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The suggestion that the ידות question is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of סוכי תאנים: the תנא קמא against אחרים.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as a dispute about handles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא this way: אחרים hold the stalks have ידות, and the תנא קמא holds they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not that they argue about this point: one master holds they have ידות, and the other master holds they do not have ידות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the ברייתא's argument is really about. It is about whether stalks used for סכך count as having ידות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אחרים count the ידות together with the food, so for them the ידות are real ידות. The תנא קמא leaves the ידות out of the food count, so for him there are no ידות. This makes the ברייתא a clean argument about the same question רבי אבא and רב מנשיא discussed.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not that? Introduces a proposed reading of a source.
They have handles. The stems count as part of the food for טומאה.

phrases.english: Is it not that they disagree about this:
that one master holds they have handles,
and the other master holds they do not have handles!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That the ידות question for סכך is an old dispute.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The difference between the תנא קמא's count (waste against food) and אחרים' count (straw against ידות plus food).

steps.title: For רבי אבא, it is certainly a dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא holds that grain cut for סכך has ידות, so he clearly sides with אחרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי אבא, it is certainly a dispute among the תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that רבי אבא has no problem here. His view simply matches אחרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבא said only grapes for wine lack ידות, so grain cut for סכך does have ידות. That is the view of אחרים in the ברייתא. Siding with one תנא against another is perfectly acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who quoted רב הונא about grapes for wine.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Abba, it is certainly a dispute of Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reading from step 16 to רבי אבא's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבא follows אחרים: grain cut for סכך has ידות.

steps.title: רב מנשיא: everyone agrees, the case is different
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא can say that all agree grain cut for סכך has no ידות. The ברייתא is about grain first cut for food and later chosen for סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רב מנשיא בר גדא, shall we say it is a dispute among the תנאים? רב מנשיא can tell you: everyone agrees that one who cuts for סכך has no ידות. Here we are dealing with a case where he cut them for eating, and then changed his mind and used them for סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that רב מנשיא needs to take a side. It moves the ברייתא to a different case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain cut in the first place for סכך has no ידות according to everyone. The ברייתא's argument is about grain cut for food, which had ידות at the start, and was only later used for סכך. אחרים hold the ידות stay. So the ברייתא never argues about רב מנשיא's case.

keyTerms.meaning: He can tell you. Introduces a defense of someone's position.
What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a narrower reading of a source.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: an אמורא avoids depending on a dispute between תנאים by reading the source as a special case.

phrases.english: According to Rav Menashya bar Gadda,
shall we say it is a dispute of Tannaim?
Rav Menashya can tell you:
everyone holds
that one who cuts for sechach has no handles.
And here, what are we dealing with?
A case where he cut them for eating,
and then changed his mind to use them for roofing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא סָבְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects applying the reading of step 16 to רב מנשיא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the claim that רב מנשיא's ruling is argued about in the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא is not about grain cut for סכך. It is about grain cut for food that was later used for סכך.

steps.title: Then why do the רבנן say no handles?
steps.stepSummary: If the grain was cut for food, it should have ידות. So why do the רבנן (the תנא קמא) ignore the ידות?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cut them for eating, what is the reason of the רבנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב מנשיא's new reading of the ברייתא. Food that was cut for eating normally has ידות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the new reading, אחרים make sense, because food cut for eating has ידות. But the תנא קמא now looks puzzling. Why would grain cut for food lose its ידות?

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages. Here, the תנא קמא of the ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he cut them for eating,
what is the reason of the Rabbis?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קְוצָצָן לַאֲכִילָה מַאי טַעְמַיְיהוּ דְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the case definition given in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב מנשיא's reading of the ברייתא as food later used for סכך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food cut for eating has ידות, so the רבנן's ruling of no ידות needs a reason.

steps.title: Suggested answer: changing his mind cancels the first plan
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the רבנן hold that once he decided to use the grain for סכך, his original plan to eat it is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say the רבנן hold that since he changed his mind about them for סכך, his first intention is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer for the רבנן, which it will test right away. The new plan wipes out the old plan.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that a new intention for סכך overrides the original food intention. Without the food intention, the stalks become plain סכך with no ידות. This is only a proposal, introduced with וכי תימא.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say. Introduces a suggested answer that will be tested.
Intention. Plays a key role in the laws of טומאה.

phrases.english: And if you say the Rabbis hold
that since he changed his mind about them for roofing,
his first intention is cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proposed reason based on cancelling the first intention.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Grain cut for food keeps its ידות even after he decides to use it for סכך.
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed only: a new intention for סכך would cancel the food intention, so there would be no ידות. The next step challenges this from the משנה about vessels.

steps.title: Can intention alone cancel? A משנה about vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether a mere change of intention can cancel the first intention, and begins quoting a משנה about vessels.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is an intention cancelled in this way? Didn't we learn in a משנה: all vessels...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested answer from step 20 and starts to bring a משנה as proof. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that thought alone may not be enough to undo an earlier status. The משנה about vessels, which continues on the next amud, teaches that status changes in טומאה can come from thought but cannot be undone by thought alone. That would mean the change of mind cannot remove the ידות.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it so? A rhetorical challenge.
But didn't we learn in a משנה?
All vessels. The opening of the quoted משנה.

phrases.english: But is an intention cancelled in this way?
But didn't we learn in a mishna: All vessels...

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי בָּטְלָה לֵיהּ מַחְשָׁבָה בְּהָכִי וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proposed answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that changing his mind to סכך cancels the original food intention.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה about vessels (continued on the next amud) shows that intention alone cannot undo an earlier status.
